instruction: Why is my EMR cluster {{troubleshooting-multiservice-emr-0hr2dw3rz-eu-west-1-EmrClusterId}} in eu-west-1 experiencing performance issues? Spark jobs are taking much longer than expected.
expected_answer: The EMR cluster {{troubleshooting-multiservice-emr-0hr2dw3rz-eu-west-1-EmrClusterId}} is experiencing performance issues due to a severe executor overallocation. The spark-defaults configuration sets spark.executor.instances to 425 with spark.executor.memory of 20G and spark.yarn.executor.memoryOverhead of 3G, totalling 23 GB per executor. While 23 GB fits within the 32 GB available on each m5.2xlarge core node, the core instance fleet only targets 1 instance, meaning YARN can provision at most 1 executor. The remaining 424 requested executors are never allocated, so the vast majority of Spark tasks are queued indefinitely. Dynamic allocation is disabled (spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled: false), so Spark cannot scale the executor count down to match actual capacity. The driver memory is also set to 60 GB (spark.driver.memory: 60G), which exceeds the total memory of an m5.2xlarge instance and will cause the driver to fail to launch. Additionally, spark.sql.shuffle.partitions is set to 3000, which adds unnecessary scheduling overhead relative to the 1 available executor.
